question: Which source supplied the May and June average waits printed in the Valley Post? Cite the sentences that trace both figures to their source.
options: The clinic’s bulletin supplied both averages.
The Echo’s own observations supplied both averages.
The clinic supplied May’s average and the Echo measured June’s.
The Echo measured May’s average and the clinic supplied June’s.

sentences: The Valley Post reported that average waiting time at Larch Clinic fell from 50 minutes in May to 35 in June.
The Post attributed both monthly figures to the clinic’s bulletin.
The neighboring Echo had printed both averages from the clinic’s bulletin on its health page.
The Echo also interviewed patients in the waiting room for that page.
variants.why: The Post identifies the bulletin as the source of both figures. The Echo’s interviews supply no separate monthly average.

sentences: The Valley Post reported that average waiting time at Larch Clinic fell from 50 minutes in May to 35 in June.
The Post attributed both monthly figures to the Echo’s health page.
The neighboring Echo had printed both averages from the clinic’s bulletin on its health page.
The Echo also interviewed patients in the waiting room for that page.
variants.why: The Post points to the Echo and the Echo points to the bulletin. The two stories share the clinic’s figures.

question: Which of the Valley Post’s two factual claims did its reporter verify firsthand? Cite the sentences that account for both claims.
options: Both the opening of the desk and the decline in average waits.
The decline in average waits alone.
The opening of the desk alone.
Neither the opening of the desk nor the decline in average waits.

sentences: The Valley Post wrote that Larch Clinic opened a second reception desk and that average waiting time fell from 50 minutes in May to 35 in June.
The reporter learned of the desk opening by phone from the clinic manager after the event.
A photograph supplied by the clinic accompanied the story.
For the decline in waits, the reporter relied entirely on the clinic’s announcement.
variants.why: The clinic supplied both the account of the opening and the numerical claim. Its photograph does not make the reporter an eyewitness.

sentences: The Valley Post wrote that Larch Clinic opened a second reception desk and that average waiting time fell from 50 minutes in May to 35 in June.
The reporter watched the second desk open and its clerk begin checking in patients.
A photograph supplied by the clinic accompanied the story.
For the decline in waits, the reporter relied entirely on the clinic’s announcement.
variants.why: The reporter saw the new desk open. The clinic still supplied the waiting-time figures, and watching the desk open does not establish what caused the decline.

question: Which underlying counts supplied the two stories’ ferry totals? Cite the links between each story, its file and the count in that file.
options: Harbor Watch used the stewards’ count and Sound Desk used the operator’s.
Both stories used the ferry operator’s turnstile count.
Both stories used the ramp stewards’ hand count.
Harbor Watch used the operator’s count and Sound Desk used the stewards’.

sentences: Harbor Watch attributed its Founders’ Day total of 412 boardings to municipal file M17.
The ramp stewards conducted a hand count of boardings that day while the ferry’s turnstile was operating.
The ferry operator invoices the city for 412 boardings on Founders’ Day without naming the file it used.
The city compiled M17 from the operator’s turnstile tape.
Sound Desk printed the same total, crediting file S4 in the pier archive.
The pier archive describes S4 as a scan of the operator’s turnstile tape.
variants.why: M17 and S4 both derive from the turnstile. The stewards made another count, but neither story used it.

sentences: Harbor Watch attributed its Founders’ Day total of 412 boardings to municipal file M17.
The ramp stewards conducted a hand count of boardings that day while the ferry’s turnstile was operating.
The ferry operator invoices the city for 412 boardings on Founders’ Day without naming the file it used.
The city compiled M17 from the operator’s turnstile tape.
Sound Desk printed the same total, crediting file S4 in the pier archive.
The pier archive describes S4 as a scan of the ramp stewards’ original hand-count sheets.
variants.why: M17 carries the turnstile reading, while S4 preserves the hand count. Equal totals and archival copies are compatible with two separate counts.

question: In the off-site recovery drill, which items did the inspector verify could be read or played? Cite the sentences establishing what she tested for each item.
options: Only the marked score.
Both the marked score and the rehearsal tape.
Only the rehearsal tape.
Neither the marked score nor the rehearsal tape.

sentences: The conservatory said a marked score could be read and a rehearsal tape could be played from its off-site backup.
In the recovery drill, the inspector opened the backup score and compared its penciled bass line with a reference photograph.
For the backup tape, she transcribed its title and duration from the catalog without playing the file.
A storage-center inventory from the previous week also listed both items.
variants.why: Reading the bass line tested the score. The title and duration came from a catalog, which says nothing about successful playback in the drill.

sentences: The conservatory said a marked score could be read and a rehearsal tape could be played from its off-site backup.
In the recovery drill, the inspector opened the backup score and compared its penciled bass line with a reference photograph.
For the backup tape, she played the file and compared its opening bars with the catalog description.
A storage-center inventory from the previous week also listed both items.
variants.why: The inspector read the score and heard the tape. Each item was usable at least to the extent exercised in the drill.

question: Which instruments supplied the crest readings published by the Northbank bulletin, Wharf Gazette and harbor club yearbook? Cite the chain for each publication.
options: The club gauge supplied the bulletin and Gazette, and the board gauge supplied the yearbook.
The board gauge supplied the bulletin, and the club gauge supplied the Gazette and yearbook.
The board gauge supplied the bulletin and Gazette, and the club gauge supplied the yearbook.
The board gauge supplied the bulletin and yearbook, and the club gauge supplied the Gazette.

sentences: The Northbank bulletin labels its 2.4-meter crest reading N-8, and the Wharf Gazette credits G-4 for its reading.
N-8 records the peak from the water board’s float gauge at Lock Eight.
The Wharf Gazette also publishes the pilot station’s tide forecast under code F-4.
The harbor club yearbook gives its crest reading under accession C-6.
G-4 is a newspaper clipping of the crest entry in N-8.
Port archive file R-2 is a microfilm image of N-8.
C-6 records the peak from the harbor club’s own gauge at the boathouse.
variants.why: G-4 copies N-8, so the two papers share the board gauge. The yearbook has the boathouse gauge as a separate source.

sentences: The Northbank bulletin labels its 2.4-meter crest reading N-8, and the Wharf Gazette credits G-4 for its reading.
N-8 records the peak from the water board’s float gauge at Lock Eight.
The Wharf Gazette also publishes the pilot station’s tide forecast under code F-4.
The harbor club yearbook gives its crest reading under accession C-6.
G-4 is a newspaper clipping of the crest entry in port archive file R-2.
Port archive file R-2 is a microfilm image of N-8.
C-6 records the peak from the harbor club’s own gauge at the boathouse.
variants.why: The Gazette’s clipping goes through R-2 to N-8 and the board gauge. The additional copy leaves the yearbook as the sole publication here using the club gauge.

question: For which loads do the auditor’s extracts verify receipt by the pantry before noon? Cite the stamp convention and the entries that settle both loads.
options: Fen alone.
Both Haw and Fen.
Neither Haw nor Fen.
Haw alone.

sentences: The carrier said its Haw and Fen loads had both reached the island pantry before noon.
For Fen the auditor copied a violet stamp timed 11:55.
Violet means a driver took custody at the depot, while green means a pantry worker took custody at the island.
The auditor’s Haw extract shows a green stamp timed 11:40.
Both extracts bear the signatures of the people who took custody.
variants.why: The green stamp puts Haw in pantry custody before noon. Fen’s violet stamp records dispatch, leaving its arrival time open.

sentences: The carrier said its Haw and Fen loads had both reached the island pantry before noon.
For Fen the auditor copied a green stamp timed 11:55.
Violet means a driver took custody at the depot, while green means a pantry worker took custody at the island.
The auditor’s Haw extract shows a green stamp timed 11:40.
Both extracts bear the signatures of the people who took custody.
variants.why: Both entries document transfer to a pantry worker, and both times precede noon.

question: Whose stall counts did the council ledger and the Beacon actually publish on August 10? Cite the issue history and the source links needed to identify both counts.
options: The ledger used the inspector’s count and the Beacon used the guild’s.
Both publications used the stallholders’ guild’s count.
The ledger used the guild’s count and the Beacon used the inspector’s.
Both publications used the market inspector’s count.

sentences: The council ledger’s August 10 entry credits tally sheet H for its 18 active stalls.
The Beacon’s August 10 story credits market sheet M as it stood at the opening bell.
The market office switched M from issue 1 to issue 2 at 3 p.m., between the opening and closing bells.
Issue 1 transcribes a separate count the stallholders’ guild made during its own circuit of the market.
The Beacon’s closing edition repeated its morning weather table with a new headline.
H contains the market inspector’s count from a walk past all the stalls.
Issue 2 reproduces H with the stall numbers rearranged in street order.
Both issues of M give the same total of 18.
variants.why: The opening-bell issue was issue 1, based on the guild’s circuit. The ledger cites H, based on the inspector’s walk.

sentences: The council ledger’s August 10 entry credits tally sheet H for its 18 active stalls.
The Beacon’s August 10 story credits market sheet M as it stood at the closing bell.
The market office switched M from issue 1 to issue 2 at 3 p.m., between the opening and closing bells.
Issue 1 transcribes a separate count the stallholders’ guild made during its own circuit of the market.
The Beacon’s closing edition repeated its morning weather table with a new headline.
H contains the market inspector’s count from a walk past all the stalls.
Issue 2 reproduces H with the stall numbers rearranged in street order.
Both issues of M give the same total of 18.
variants.why: The closing-bell issue was issue 2, a reordered copy of H. Both publications therefore use the inspector’s walk, although the guild also counted the stalls.

question: Which chair shipments qualify under the council’s witness rule on this record? Cite the rule and the records needed to evaluate each shipment.
options: Both Bay and Hill.
Hill alone.
Bay alone.
Neither Bay nor Hill.

sentences: A shipment qualified only through a witnessed run in which its own sample sustained at least 120 kilograms for 60 consecutive seconds.
The receiving book identifies chair J as Bay’s shipment sample and chair K as Hill’s.
The only runs the witness attended and signed were 41 with chair J and 42 with chair K.
The logger recorded run 41 at 125 kilograms for 70 continuous seconds.
The manufacturer’s certificate rates both chairs for 130 kilograms in routine use.
Run 42 held 122 kilograms for 35 seconds, dipped to 118 for 5 seconds and held 122 for 35 more before the run ended.
The operator also credited Hill with an uninterrupted 90-second run at 125 kilograms on run sheet 43.
variants.why: Bay’s signed run clears both thresholds. Hill’s signed run never stays above the minimum for a full minute. Run 43 lacks the required witness.

sentences: A shipment qualified only through a witnessed run in which its own sample sustained at least 120 kilograms for 60 consecutive seconds.
The receiving book identifies chair J as Bay’s shipment sample and chair K as Hill’s.
The only runs the witness attended and signed were 41 with chair J and 42 with chair K.
The logger recorded run 41 at 125 kilograms for 70 continuous seconds.
The manufacturer’s certificate rates both chairs for 130 kilograms in routine use.
Run 42 held 122 kilograms for 35 seconds, rose to 124 for 5 seconds and held 122 for 35 more before the run ended.
The operator also credited Hill with an uninterrupted 90-second run at 125 kilograms on run sheet 43.
variants.why: Bay clears the thresholds in run 41. All 75 seconds of Hill’s signed run 42 meet the load minimum, including the five seconds at 124 kilograms.

question: Which accounts trace their east-passage width to a field measurement of that passage made after the rehang? Cite the records that date and identify each account’s underlying reading.
options: Both the works office and the tenants’ bulletin.
The works office alone.
Neither the works office nor the tenants’ bulletin.
The tenants’ bulletin alone.

sentences: The crew completed the rehang of both terminal doors at 4 p.m. on Tuesday, May 13.
For the reported east-passage width, the works office credits card P-14 and the tenants’ bulletin credits card M-32.
P-14 transcribes the surveyor’s tape reading in the east passage at 9 a.m. on Tuesday, May 13.
The works office dated the fair copy of P-14 on the morning after the rehang.
The survey register assigns station 9 to the east passage and station 7 to the west passage.
The return visit at 10 a.m. on Wednesday, May 14, produced the field cards in series M.
On M-32 the surveyor entered a fresh tape reading for station 9 and copied the pre-rehang reading for station 7.
variants.why: P-14’s reading predates completion. M-32 contains a fresh reading at east station 9 from the next morning, so only the bulletin reaches a post-rehang measurement of that passage.

sentences: The crew completed the rehang of both terminal doors at 4 p.m. on Tuesday, May 13.
For the reported east-passage width, the works office credits card P-14 and the tenants’ bulletin credits card M-32.
P-14 transcribes the surveyor’s tape reading in the east passage at 9 a.m. on Tuesday, May 13.
The works office dated the fair copy of P-14 on the morning after the rehang.
The survey register assigns station 9 to the east passage and station 7 to the west passage.
The return visit at 10 a.m. on Wednesday, May 14, produced the field cards in series M.
On M-32 the surveyor entered a fresh tape reading for station 7 and copied the pre-rehang reading for station 9.
variants.why: The works office reaches Tuesday morning’s reading, and the bulletin reaches the old reading copied for east station 9. Reissuing that value on a field card does not date the underlying measurement to the return visit.

question: Which of the town’s two claimed minimum counts could the dinner examiner verify from the records? Cite the sentences needed to assess both counts.
options: The minimum count of ward residents alone.
The minimum count of distinct guests alone.
Both the minimum guest count and the minimum ward-resident count.
Neither the minimum guest count nor the minimum ward-resident count.

sentences: The town said Thursday’s dinner drew at least 100 distinct guests, at least 70 of whom lived in the ward.
The examiner counted 108 admission stubs in the box at the door.
The catering invoice lists 119 dinners served that evening, including second helpings.
After merging stubs bearing the same wristband number, the examiner counted 102 different numbers.
The door clerk certified that each guest received just one numbered wristband for the evening and could deposit stubs only for that band.
The sole address record was a survey with 76 responses giving an in-ward home address on forms that carried no guest identifiers and allowed repeat submissions.
variants.why: The 102 different numbers require at least 102 guests under the clerk’s one-band rule. The anonymous responses may include repeats, so 76 forms cannot verify 70 distinct residents.

sentences: The town said Thursday’s dinner drew at least 100 distinct guests, at least 70 of whom lived in the ward.
The examiner counted 108 admission stubs in the box at the door.
The catering invoice lists 119 dinners served that evening, including second helpings.
After merging stubs bearing the same wristband number, the examiner counted 102 different numbers.
The door clerk certified that each guest received just one numbered wristband for the evening and could deposit stubs only for that band.
The sole address record was a survey linking 76 different guest wristbands to in-ward addresses given in response to a request for the address of each guest’s host.
variants.why: The one-band rule and 102 different numbers verify the guest minimum. The 76 linked addresses locate hosts, so the record cannot establish that 70 guests themselves lived in the ward.
